newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Austalian gold index sidelined in range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Austalian gold index sidelined in range.

text.p: --------------Analysis by Daniel Fock - May 16--------------
*Index to move sideways within range 1,535 to 1,610
*Indicators oversold longer term but lower short term.
*Traders likely to proceed with caution.
*Gold index closed at 1,573.3 Thursday
The Australian gold index has traded higher but is down to test interim support at 1,565/60.
There is some concern as short term leading indicators are turning over, but the index is still within consolidation range 1,535 to 1,610.
Traders will remain sceptical with the bears able to bite at any time.
Short term technicals are mixed. The averages are bullish except for the 40 day.
The ROC and RSI have moved higher but after a short sideways phase are starting to move lower.
The Stochastics are higher but the faster indicators could drop lower throught the slower and traders will be cautious.
In the medium term, the index is seen above last week's levels but is testing interim support at 1,565/60.
The index is still in the bear channel so medium term bears will tighten trailling stops on shorts, especially if the index can rally above 1,610.
Medium term technicals are bearish and very oversold. Averages are bearish.
Leading indicators have been very oversold and trading sideways but this week they have turned slightly higher.
The Stochastics are extremely oversold and level at 10.
While support at 1,540/35 holds, previous Fibonacci levels remain at 1,717, 1,771, and 1,826.

In the longer term, the index continues lower within its bear corridor. Bears continue to focus on the head and shoulders formation but with the oversold nature of the index, they too will be cautious and move trailling stops closer to current levels.
Longer term technicals are bearish and oversold. Averages remain bearish but leading indicators are losing bearish momentum.
All leading indicators are slightly higher than last weeks levels.
The index has bounced from support at 1,540, rallied close to resistance at 1,610, but reached only 1,593 and is now testing interim support at 1,565/60.
Traders will be trading the range and the breaks.
The index has been falling for 14 months without a decent correction.
The bears are still in control, but for how long is the question.
The current price action could be a corrective movement and hence there is a growing possibility of an upward move.
Technicals are conflicting so traders are likely to use price points, 1,535/1,565/1,610 as their marks.
(Daniel Fock is a member of the Australian Technical Analysts Association. Views are his own.)
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
